neighbours.label: the piece that completes certain multi-token English surnames and place names: Cool-idge, Coler-idge, Full-erton, Cull-oden, Cl-ither-ow, Pink-erton
fire: Calvin Coolidge became president after Harding died in 1923.
We read a poem by Coleridge in class this morning.
The college in Fullerton enrolled a record number of students.
The Jacobite army was destroyed at Culloden on a cold April day.
A shrine to Margaret Clitherow stands in a narrow street in York.
The guards were hired from the Pinkerton agency.
Grace Coolidge kept a pet raccoon at the White House.
Wordsworth and Coleridge walked together in the Quantock hills.
quiet: Warren Harding became president after Wilson left office in 1921.
We read a poem by Wordsworth in class this morning.
The college in Edgerton enrolled a record number of students.
The royal army was destroyed at Hastings on an October day.
A shrine to Thomas Becket stands in the cathedral at Canterbury.
The guards were hired from the Aldridge agency.
Eleanor Roosevelt kept a small dog at the White House.
Lord Woolton and Mr. Routledge walked together in the hills.

notes: Probes: Coolidge 0.99, Coleridge 1.00, Fullerton 0.94, Culloden 0.88, Clitherow 0.80, Cullompton 0.53, Pinkerton 0.43, Crittenden 0.36. The same suffixes after other stems stayed quiet: Edgerton 0.05, Aldridge 0.06, Atherton/Wolverton 0.16, Woolton 0.01, Routledge 0.03. So the stem matters (Cool-, Coler-, Full-, Cull-), and the label is a list of names, not a suffix rule.
